evidences.text: pwc.blogs.com Updated Apr 27th, 2015 Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests 27 April 2015 Follow @tlansec Executive Summary This short report details the techniques being used in a series of attacks mostly against Israel­based organisations.

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: Pomf.se is a relatively low­profile file sharing/hosting website currently based in Sweden.

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: DownExecute – Brief Analysis We’ve chosen to refer to the malware as ‘DownExecute’ due to the .pdb string left in the malware (leaving debug paths in malware seems to be very fashionable at the moment…):

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: The DownExecute malware is used as a way for the attackers to gain an initial foothold on the victim machine.

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: We don’t have great visibility into post­compromise activity at this stage; however there are a number of other malware samples which communicate with the same infrastructure as the DownExecute samples.

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: It’s not unreasonable to infer that if these are more fully featured backdoors, that they are likely the 2 nd stage malware families used in conjunction with DownExecute.

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: Specifically, we’ve observed the well­ documented Xtreme RAT and Poison Ivy malware families in use with the same domain names as DownExecute.

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: The Poison Ivy passwords observed for the group were ‘admin2014’ and ‘admin!@#$%”.

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: The vast majority of infrastructure in terms of hostnames observed associated with these attacks have been dynamic DNS domains, primarily associated with no­ip.com.

evidences.text: So do we believe this campaign is focused only at Israeli companies?

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: Whilst this is a subject which is clearly of key interest to all parties in the region, the fact the attackers sent an Arabic language version of the story may indicate that the recipient was expected to be fluent in Arabic, and possibly therefore less likely to be Israeli, but rather

evidences.text: Password schema: In their August 2013 blog [7] , FireEye noted that a group they refer to as MoleRats used Poison Ivy and Xtreme RAT, in conjunction with a password of “!@#GooD#@!” The keyboard walk used for the symbols “!@#” across the top of a keyboard is similar to the password observed in some of our Poison Ivy samples.

evidences.report_id: Attacks against Israeli & Palestinian interests - Cyber security updates
evidences.text: The fact that the attackers chose to develop their own dropper may be indicative that their biggest problem when conducting network intrusions is getting their foot in the door – particularly as it seems as though they still prefer the more fully featured Poison Ivy and Xtreme RAT backdoors as 2 nd stage malware families.
